$comment: Secrets never go on a command line. An argument is in the program's argv, which /proc/<pid>/cmdline shows to every process on the runner while it runs, so a token passed as -p/--password/--creds/--registry-password, inside a user:$TOKEN@ URL, or to an action input the action turns into such a flag, can be read by anything else on the build host. Hand it over on stdin instead (printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | podman login ... --password-stdin), write it to a file (printf ... > file), or log in first with docker/login-action, which reads the password on stdin. Scans the run: scripts of every workflow and the inputs listed in actionInputs. A value is secret-bearing when it references a variable whose name contains TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSWD or SECRET (any case), or a ${{ }} expression that does (secrets.*, github.token). Evaluated by scripts/check-policies.mjs; explained in policies/README.md and docs/security/SECURITY-AI.md section 2.
